channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan to consolidate work of local authorities, banks under deputy prime minister
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to hold weekly meetings chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister for work with mahallas to discuss issues related to their activities. A new position, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Association of Uzbek Mahallas, has been established and filled. This official will coordinate the work of local authorities, district organizations, and banks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Significantly Reduces Poverty Rates Ahead of Schedule
item.description: Uzbekistan is reducing poverty faster than projected, with the poverty rate falling from 17% in 2021 to an estimated 4.5% by 2026. This decline is attributed to job creation, entrepreneurship support, and increased use of household plots for income, alongside reduced inequality.

item.title: Bukhara Region and USA Expand Economic and Tourism Ties
item.description: The Bukhara region of Uzbekistan and the United States are strengthening economic and tourism cooperation. Discussions between the regional governor and the US deputy ambassador focused on investment potential, economic opportunities, tourism resources, and ongoing joint projects in agriculture and education.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Reviews Employment and Income Growth Initiatives
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev critically reviewed regional efforts to boost employment and increase public income. A new system assigns regional and district-level responsibilities to khokims, with employment agencies and economic structures tasked with local job creation and income enhancement. Some officials were noted for failing to engage directly with communities and businesses.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Regulate Illegally Occupied Land Around Apartment Buildings
item.description: Uzbekistan may offer land plots for private kindergartens, schools, and technical schools at a starting price of 1 million soums for auction if entrepreneurs commit to educating children from needy families for free. This initiative aims to provide employment for parents and quality education for children.

item.title: Building Valued at $1.2 Million Returned to State Ownership in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A building and a 23,500 square meter land plot in Naryn, Kyrgyzstan, valued at approximately 96.5 million soms (about $1.2 million), have been returned to state ownership. The property was illegally transferred to private hands in 2003 by officials violating land legislation.

item.title: Canada Imposes 50% Tariffs on US Goods in Response to US Trade Measures
item.description: Canada has imposed tariffs of up to 50% on US products starting September 8, retaliating against US President Donald Trump's administration's decision to levy 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. The measures cover approximately CAD 27.6 billion in imports and include steel, aluminum, dairy, and electronics.

item.title: Uzbekistan's growing international interest highlighted by foreign media
item.description: Foreign media partners have focused on Uzbekistan's developments, including economic activity, tourism, and digital transformation. Publications from Anadolu and TASS noted the establishment of a strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Serbia, with leaders signing a joint declaration and agreements on cooperation in agriculture, tourism, and culture.

item.title: SCO cooperation in AI can shape a shared digital future, referencing Al-Khwarizmi
item.description: The Bishkek Declaration calls for safe and responsible AI use, ensuring it does not harm human life or undermine state sovereignty. Uzbekistan's IT Park representative highlighted the region's historical connection to AI through mathematician Al-Khwarizmi, whose work on algorithms is foundational to modern AI development.

item.title: Uzbekistan may allow first-floor apartments for business without reclassification
item.description: Uzbekistan proposes allowing the use of first-floor apartments in multi-story buildings for commercial purposes without reclassifying them as non-residential. This aims to facilitate small businesses like shops and service centers, simplifying the current complex process of obtaining permits.

item.title: SCO summit in Bishkek expands agenda beyond security to economic cooperation
item.description: The 25th anniversary Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek marked a significant milestone, expanding its focus beyond traditional security issues. Discussions included trade, economic cooperation, investment, transport, energy, digitalization, and artificial intelligence, reflecting a comprehensive approach to Eurasian development. The summit reaffirmed the 'Shanghai Spirit' of mutual trust and consensus.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares application for Global Alliance on Vaccines and Immunization
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing its country application for support from the Global Alliance on Vaccines and Immunization (GAVI) for the 2026-2030 period. A GAVI mission visited Bishkek for a working group meeting on the application, attended by health officials and representatives from WHO and UNICEF.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares application for Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization support
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing a country application for support from the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization (GAVI) for the 2026-2030 period. A working group meeting, attended by health officials and international partners, discussed the application for GAVI 6.0 funding.

item.title: Spanish investors explore opening four and five-star hotels in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Tourism Committee met with Barceló Hotel Group to discuss tourism development. The Spanish company is interested in building four and five-star hotels and managing existing tourist facilities. This interest highlights Uzbekistan's growing attractiveness to foreign investors and its tourism potential.

item.title: German company sees rapid development in Uzbekistan's textile industry
item.description: Thomas Gnoht of Optibelt GmbH expressed interest in Uzbekistan's dynamic economic reforms, particularly in the textile sector. The company, a supplier of drive belts, sees Uzbekistan as a promising market and plans to expand cooperation and sales. They are pleased with the rapid growth of the textile industry.

item.title: Brent crude oil price surpasses $100 per barrel for first time since July
item.description: Brent crude oil futures on the ICE exchange in London traded above $100 per barrel on September 9. The price increase of over 2 percent for November delivery is attributed to renewed tensions between the US and Iran, raising concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.

item.title: Brent crude oil price surpasses $100 per barrel for first time since July
item.description: Brent crude oil futures traded above $100 per barrel on September 9, marking the first time since July 24. The price increase of over 2 percent is attributed to renewed tensions between the US and Iran, raising concerns about potential supply disruptions from the Middle East.

item.title: Kyrgyz activist claims authorities attempted to arrest him in Cambodia
item.description: Political blogger and activist Syrgak Kenzhebaev stated that Kyrgyz authorities attempted to arrest him in Cambodia on August 31. Previously, he released a video alleging that the president's brother and relatives are involved in political matters and customs in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia preparing zero-tariff free trade agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and Serbia have begun work on a free trade agreement that will establish zero tariff rates for goods on a mutual basis. The agreement is expected to create favorable conditions for Uzbek products in the Serbian market. Both countries have also adopted a separate program for industrial cooperation.

item.title: Social tax reduced to 2% for businesses hiring needy families in rural areas
item.description: Businesses in rural districts that hire members of needy families will pay a social tax of 2%. The government is prepared to offer state land plots via auction at a starting price of 1 million Uzbek soums for entrepreneurs who wish to provide free education to children from needy families.

item.title: Serbia Plans to Open Embassy in Uzbekistan to Simplify Visa Procedures
item.description: Serbia intends to establish an embassy in Uzbekistan, which could significantly simplify visa application processes for Serbian citizens. The two countries also agreed to prepare an intergovernmental agreement on migration and labor mobility. Serbia expressed interest in attracting skilled Uzbek specialists for the EXPO 2027 construction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Certify Locally-Fed Fish for Uninterrupted Export to Russia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has been instructed to complete certification procedures for fish raised on domestic feed to ensure uninterrupted export to Russia. The Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry stated this aims to support local producers and reduce reliance on foreign feed. A ban on fish feed imports is currently in effect.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prioritizes certification for fish exports to Russia using local feed
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has been instructed to complete necessary certification procedures to ensure uninterrupted fish exports to Russia, utilizing domestically produced feed. This initiative aims to support local producers and reduce reliance on foreign supplies. A six-month ban on imported fish feed is currently in effect in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan to Collaborate on Joint Pharmaceutical Research
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan will conduct joint research in the pharmaceutical sector following a memorandum of understanding signed by their respective state enterprise directors. Cooperation will focus on knowledge exchange, promoting trade and investment, modernizing production, joint research, and innovation, and participating in international events.

item.title: 81st session of UN General Assembly opens in New York
item.description: The 81st session of the UN General Assembly has opened at UN Headquarters in New York. Bangladesh diplomat Halilur Rahman became the new president. UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that restoring trust in the multilateral system is a key task. He emphasized that strengthening international cooperation is crucial to counter global challenges.

item.title: North Korea Constructs New Facilities for Uranium Enrichment at Yongbyon, IAEA Reports
item.description: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has reported that North Korea has built a new building at its Yongbyon nuclear facility capable of housing up to 28 centrifuges for uranium enrichment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Energy Ministry Not Considering Electricity Supply Restrictions
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Energy is not currently planning to restrict electricity supplies, according to ministry head Altynbek Rysbekov. A redistribution program is in place for potential shortages. The Toktogul reservoir holds 11.2 billion cubic meters of water, with a target of 11.5 billion by autumn. Plans include importing electricity from neighboring countries by 2026.

item.title: Ambassador: Xi Jinping's Visit to Kyrgyzstan Was Highly Productive
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Kyrgyzstan from August 30 to September 1 was highly productive, according to Chinese Ambassador Liu Jiangping. The leaders reached broad consensus on deepening political, economic, humanitarian, and security cooperation. They signed the Treaty on Everlasting Good-Neighborliness, Friendship and Cooperation and over 30 other documents covering trade, transport, and technology.

item.title: Court Rejects Defense's Request to Question Witnesses in Mahabat Tajibek Kyzy Case
item.description: The Lenin District Court in Bishkek rejected the defense's request to question witnesses in the case of journalist Mahabat Tajibek Kyzy, deeming it premature. The court proceeded with questioning Tajibek Kyzy first, despite the defense's objection. The next hearing is scheduled for September 15. Tajibek Kyzy was previously sentenced to six years but is now under travel restrictions pending retrial.

item.title: Kazakhstan Declares 2026 Year of Digitalization and AI, Featuring Cybersecurity Conference
item.description: Kazakhstan has declared 2026 the Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence, highlighted by 'AI Month' from September 23 to October 23. This period includes the international forum 'AI & Digital Bridge 2026' and the KazHackStan 2026 cybersecurity conference.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes three-year prison sentence for unauthorized burials
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering introducing criminal liability for unauthorized burials, exhumations, and reburials without proper permission. Proposed amendments to the Criminal Code suggest penalties including fines, community service, or up to three years imprisonment for such acts. The changes aim to address issues like sanitary violations and obscured crime concealment.

item.title: Woman reports domestic violence by police officer husband in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A resident of Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region claims she suffered years of domestic violence from her husband, a police captain. After a recent assault, she reported the abuse but fears an unfair investigation due to his position. Authorities confirmed an investigation is underway, with medical examinations conducted.

item.title: Uzbek Citizens Returning from Abroad Eligible for Grants Up to 60 Million Soums for Business Development
item.description: Uzbek citizens returning from working abroad can receive grants of up to 60 million soums to start or develop a business. Priority will be given to well-founded business ideas and proposals that create new jobs.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Strengthen State Control Over Energy Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan's "Uzenergoinspeksiya" held a meeting to enhance state control in the energy sector and promote rational energy resource use. Priorities include preventing wasteful consumption, ensuring transparency in control measures, and combating corruption. Tasks were assigned to improve energy saving culture, audits, and digital technology integration in state control processes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan to collaborate on joint pharmaceutical research
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's 'Kyrgyzpharmatsiya' state enterprise and Uzbekistan's Agency for Pharmaceutical Industry Development have signed a memorandum of understanding. The agreement focuses on knowledge exchange, promoting trade and investment, modernizing production, joint research, and innovation. The cooperation is set for three years with automatic renewal.

item.title: Uzbekistan's PISA 2025 results show decline in global student performance
item.description: Uzbekistan presented its PISA 2025 results, coinciding with the OECD's global announcement. The international assessment, focusing on science literacy this year, revealed a worldwide decline in student performance across science, reading, and math since 2000. Uzbekistan participated for the second time, with research conducted last April-May.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan imposes six-month ban on imported fish feed to boost local production
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will temporarily ban fish feed imports for six months starting September 10 to support domestic production and aquaculture. The country has four plants with a capacity of 70,000 tons annually. The Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry reported this measure aims to reduce import dependence.

item.title: Uzbekistan's gold and foreign exchange reserves increased by $7.8 billion in August
item.description: Uzbekistan's gold and foreign exchange reserves grew by $7.8 billion in August, primarily due to rising gold prices, according to the Central Bank. Gold exports decreased while accumulation increased, leading to a 12% rise in gold reserves over eight months.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Urges Citizens to Learn from Past Mistakes and Avoid Protests
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has called on citizens to learn from past mistakes and take responsibility for their words, warning against organizing protests. This marks the second time in two months that the president has issued such a statement, emphasizing accountability for criticism of the authorities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Implement 'Barnahus' System for Child Victims of Violence
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to implement the 'Barnahus' system, a child-centered model for children who are victims or witnesses of violence. The system aims to provide a safe and coordinated environment, preventing children from repeatedly recounting traumatic experiences to different agencies. This initiative is supported by the Prosecutor General's Office, the National Social Protection Agency, and UNICEF.
